status.numerical_agreement_basis: Assessed on the two produced in-scope targets, PHOENIX14-T dev and test (Table I); PHOENIX14 and CSL-Daily are out of scope (restricted by the assigning user). Reproduced dev 17.5 vs published 17.4 (+0.1) and test 19.4 vs 18.6 (+0.8) WER, from one seed-0 run stopped at 63 of 70 epochs with the checkpoint chosen on dev and test scored once. The paper reports one number per cell without seeds or variance. Basis for 'agrees': both values fall within 1 WER point of the paper, dev essentially exactly; the test gap is small next to the ordering margins in Table I (CVSign's claimed test lead over TCNet is 0.8; our 19.4 would tie TCNet's 19.4 and sit behind SignGraph's 19.1 and TwoStream-SLR's 19.3, while our dev 17.5 stays below every Table I baseline), so a reviewer may read the test value as not supporting the paper's state-of-the-art claim on that split. The tolerance is the agent's judgement, not a paper-provided criterion; unstated CCA/CVA details (C_hid, heads, Eq. 5 scaling, Conv_Block norm) are guesses that could move either number.
status.preference_level_basis: CVSign's own modules (CCA, CVA) have no published code and are implemented from the paper (level 3). Everything CVSign says it borrows runs as pinned published code with minimal patches (level 2): the CorrNet harness, TLP's temporal decoder, the VAC/SMKD losses and shared classifier, decoding and scoring.

runs.command: local CPU audit of scripts/model.py: torch.utils.flop_counter FLOP accounting and output-equivalence tests of the committed frame-scheduling against a halo-free schedule; no Modal/GPU resources used

terminal.detail: Audit of the frame scheduling that produced the run preflight-phoenix14t-001 throughput figure, prompted by a user review question about the ~207 GPU-hour estimate. Two defects found in scripts/model.py, both in our own scheduling code rather than in CVSign's method. (1) Redundant halo computation: _chunked_stage ran each temporal chunk as [start-n, start+chunk+n] with chunk=8 and n=4, pushing 16 frames through the ResNet stage, CCA and CVA and discarding 8, for each of layers 2/3/4. Measured with torch.utils.flop_counter at the realistic shape (T=140 frames, 224px): 18.5 GFLOP/frame forward versus 10.2 GFLOP/frame for identical outputs, i.e. 1.81x of the encoder's forward work was discarded. (2) The halo made results depend on a knob documented as inert: the ResNet stages and CVA's Conv_Block carry BatchNorm, so chunk boundaries silently redefined every normalization batch (B*(chunk+2n)=32 frames per chunk, frames double-counted across chunks). Measured on the committed code, changing frame_chunk_size from 4 to 16 changed the training-mode encoder output by 1.47 absolute on a feature scale of 107, about 1.4 percent. Fix applied and verified: each ResNet stage now runs once over all real frames of the batch (the paper's visual encoder is a 2D CNN, Fig. 2, so this is exact); CVA runs unchunked per clip inside a single gradient checkpoint, keeping its Conv_Block normalization batch intact; CCA chunks only its affinity matrix, which is exact because CCA contains no normalization layer. Padded timesteps are no longer computed at all: the encoder now consumes each clip's `lengths[i]` real frames, so the zero frames that batch size 2 forces on unequal-length clips no longer enter any BatchNorm. Paper compatibility checked before applying: Eq. 1's sliding window has stride 1 over the whole video; Eq. 8's Conv_Block has kernel 1x3x3 and Eqs. 6/9 use Conv_1x1x1, so every operation downstream of the window is temporally pointwise and computing a sub-range of output positions is exactly equivalent; the paper defines V = {v_t} with exactly T frames and never introduces padding frames. gates.reason: Run scheduling-audit-001 changed how scripts/model.py schedules frames through the visual encoder, before any full run. The change is behaviour-affecting and therefore gated: the committed code's training-mode output depended on frame_chunk_size, a parameter its own docstring described as a pure memory knob, because chunk boundaries redefined the BatchNorm batch of every ResNet stage and of CVA's Conv_Block; and the encoder computed the zero frames that batch size 2 forces on unequal-length clips, letting them into those same normalization statistics. The fix removes both dependences rather than introducing a new choice: ResNet stages run once over all real frames of the batch, CVA runs unchunked per clip, CCA chunks only its affinity matrix (it has no normalization layer, so this is exact at any chunk size), and padded timesteps are not computed. It is compatible with the paper's own equations and makes the implementation less dependent on unstated choices than before.
